firstFinal:
The old test did depend on `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT`, and the fixed one doesn't.

I ran `squeal proof scripts/release-identity.test.mjs --base HEAD~1 --case test --env GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT=2`. It runs the test file from before the fix and the test file from the fix against the same product code, with `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT=2` set, as on a CI re-run.

- **Old test (`HEAD~1`) fails with the variable set to 2.** The release versions come out with an extra attempt suffix:
  - nightly: got `1.2.3-nightly.20261108.9.2`, expected `1.2.3-nightly.20261108.9`
  - PR: got `1.2.3-pr7.9.2`, expected `1.2.3-pr7.9`
- **Fixed test (`HEAD`) passes under the same variable.**
- **Old test passes without the variable.** Squeal's report shows it passing with `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT` unset, which is why the failure only appeared on re-runs.

The verdict was "1 proven", from 3 runs.

The cause is in the test's `run()` helper, which strips workflow variables from `process.env` before spawning the release script. The old filter only removed `GITHUB_ACTIONS`, so `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT` leaked through whenever CI set it. The fix changes the filter to drop every `GITHUB_*` variable. It also sets `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT: '1'` explicitly in the spawned environment, so the expected versions no longer depend on the host.

I haven't tested the fixed test under other `GITHUB_*` variables, such as `GITHUB_SHA`. The new filter removes them all, so I'd expect it to hold, but the proof only covered `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT`.
